Food and water ### Famine These paragraphs are an excerpt from [Gaza Strip famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip_famine "Gaza Strip famine").\[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gaza_Strip_famine&action=edit)\] The population of the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip") underwent a [famine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Famine "Famine") as a result of an [Israeli blockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)") during the [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") between 22 August 2025 and 19 December 2025.[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-22)[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_reuters20251219-23) The prevention of basic essentials and [humanitarian aid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitarian_aid_during_the_Gaza_war "Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war") from entering Gaza,[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-24)[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-25)[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_un20240318-26) as well as [airstrikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_bombing_of_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip") that destroyed food infrastructure, such as bakeries, mills, and food stores, caused a widespread scarcity of essential supplies.[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-28) Humanitarian aid was also blocked by [protests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_blockade_of_aid_delivery_to_the_Gaza_Strip "Israeli blockade of aid delivery to the Gaza Strip") at borders and ports. Increasing [societal breakdown in Gaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Societal_breakdown_in_the_Gaza_Strip_during_the_Gaza_war "Societal breakdown in the Gaza Strip during the Gaza war"), including looting, was also cited as a barrier to the provision of aid. By August 2025, [Integrated Food Security Phase Classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_Food_Security_Phase_Classification "Integrated Food Security Phase Classification") (IPC) projections showed that 100% of the population are experiencing "high levels of acute food insecurity", and 32% were projected to face Phase 5 catastrophic levels by 30 September 2025.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_IPC_22_August_2025-29) On 22 August 2025, the IPC said that famine is taking place in at least one of the five [governorates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governorates_of_Palestine "Governorates of Palestine") in the Gaza Strip: specifically, the [Gaza Governorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Governorate "Gaza Governorate") which includes [Gaza City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_City "Gaza City"). The IPC added that, within the next month, famine was likely to also occur in both the [Deir al-Balah Governorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deir_al-Balah_Governorate "Deir al-Balah Governorate") and the [Khan Yunis Governorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khan_Yunis_Governorate "Khan Yunis Governorate"). The IPC had insufficient data on the [North Gaza Governorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Gaza_Governorate "North Gaza Governorate") for a classification but concluded that conditions were likely similar or worse than in the Gaza Governorate.[\[27\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_IPC_22_August_2025-29)[\[28\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_reuters20250822-30) Within the next 6 weeks as of 16 August, the number of people in IPC Phase 5 was expected to rise from 500,000 to over 640,000.[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-31) On 22 October 2025, the [International Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice") found that Israel is obliged to guarantee sufficient food to Gazans and to allow [UNRWA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNRWA "UNRWA") to operate in Gaza.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_ICJ_2025Oct22_obligations_IL-32) On 19 December, the IPC published a report declaring that there is no longer a famine in Gaza after improvements in food delivery following the ceasefire, but warned that the situation remains "highly fragile" with 100,000 still facing "catastrophic conditions", although that number was projected to decline to 1,900 by April 2026.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_reuters20251219-23)[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Gaza_Strip_famine_apnews20251219-33) As of January 2026, Gazans have received enough humanitarian aid to meet their basic food needs for the first time since the start of the war.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-34) However, in late July 2026, the IPC reported that the scale-up of humanitarian assistance, enabled by improved access and reduced conflict intensity following the October 2025 ceasefire announcement, has driven improvements in food security and nutrition conditions across Gaza. At the same, the report indicated that over 1.2 million people (59% of the population of Gaza) continued to face Phase 3 Crisis levels of food insecurity or worse, including 212,000 (about 10% of Gazans) experiencing Phase 4 Emergency levels, and warned that Gaza is still experiencing a severe food emergency that could develop into another famine.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-35)[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-36) Initial block on aid > The amount of aid coming in is a drop in the bucket of Gaza’s humanitarian needs. Before this conflict, about 100 trucks of aid alone entered Gaza \[a day\]. So imagine now, with all the hostilities going on, if only this number is coming in. —Mey al Sayegh, ( [Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_Red_Cross_and_Red_Crescent_Societies "International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies"))[\[450\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-461) On 9 October, Israel implemented a [complete blockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_blockade_of_the_Gaza_Strip_(2023%E2%80%93present) "Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)") on Gaza, preventing the entry of any humanitarian aid.[\[451\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-462) Egypt closed its border to prevent civilians fleeing, but said that it would allow aid to be delivered through the [Rafah crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafah_crossing "Rafah crossing").[\[452\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-463) A week later, despite international calls for deliveries, hundreds of tons of aid were stuck on Egypt's side of the border, as Israel bombarded the crossing amid fears of weapons deliveries, and declined to assure Egyptian authorities it would pause airstrikes for civilian aid convoys.[\[453\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-464)[\[454\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-465) In Israel, aid to Gaza was reportedly prevented by far-right politicians allied with Netanyahu.[\[455\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-466) On 17 October, the UNRWA stated that there was currently "no water or electricity in Gaza. Soon there will be no food or medicine either".[\[456\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-467)[\[457\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-468) ### Deliveries to southern Gaza On 18 October, Israel announced it would allow food, water, and medicine to be delivered to a "safe zone" in west [Khan Younis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khan_Younis "Khan Younis") in southern Gaza, distributed by the United Nations.[\[458\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Israel_says_it_will_allow_Egypt-469)[\[49\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Joe_Biden_warns_Israel-51)[\[459\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-470) Later the same day, US president [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden") announced Egypt agreed to allow 20 trucks with aid to enter Gaza by 20 October.[\[460\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-471)[\[461\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-472) More than 100 trucks of aid were waiting at the Rafah crossing to enter into Gaza.[\[462\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-473) In a statement, [Human Rights Watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Rights_Watch "Human Rights Watch") stated that without electricity or fuel, however, the provided aid would fail "meeting the needs of Gaza's population".[\[463\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-474)[\[458\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Israel_says_it_will_allow_Egypt-469) On 19 October, US Special Envoy [David M. Impact on children [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Damage_in_Gaza_Strip_during_the_October_2023_-_45.jpg/250px-Damage_in_Gaza_Strip_during_the_October_2023_-_45.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Damage_in_Gaza_Strip_during_the_October_2023_-_45.jpg) Wounded infant at Al-Shifa Hospital, 11 October 2023 This section is an excerpt from [Effect of the Gaza war on children in the Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effect_of_the_Gaza_war_on_children_in_the_Gaza_Strip "Effect of the Gaza war on children in the Gaza Strip").\[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Effect_of_the_Gaza_war_on_children_in_the_Gaza_Strip&action=edit)\] [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ca/Boys_salvaging_a_destroyed_building_in_the_Gaza_Strip.jpg/250px-Boys_salvaging_a_destroyed_building_in_the_Gaza_Strip.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boys_salvaging_a_destroyed_building_in_the_Gaza_Strip.jpg) Boys salvaging a destroyed building in the Gaza Strip The [Gaza war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") has disproportionately affected children, who make up about 40% of the population of the [Gaza Strip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip "Gaza Strip").[\[520\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-532) In November 2023, [UN Secretary General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations") [António Guterres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant%C3%B3nio_Guterres "António Guterres") warned that "Gaza is becoming a graveyard for children. Hundreds of girls and boys are reportedly being killed or injured every day."[\[521\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-533) As the war continued, the toll increased steadily, reaching at least 19,424 children by 3 September 2025.[\[522\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Effect_of_the_Gaza_war_on_children_in_the_Gaza_Strip_hums42-534) Within the first month of the war, about 700,000 children in Gaza had been [displaced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forced_displacement "Forced displacement").[\[523\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-535)[\[524\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-536) A May 2025 estimate reports that 1.9 million people, roughly 90% of Gaza's population, had been displaced by the war. Many had been uprooted repeatedly, in some cases more than ten times.[\[525\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-537) The collapse of essential services created a humanitarian crisis, as families struggled to access food, clean water, and medical care. The ongoing crisis also impacted routine vaccinations, leaving thousands of children at risk of preventable disease. Additional hardships included inadequate shelter, a lack of adequate winter clothing, and the continuing psychological toll on children's mental health.[\[526\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-Effect_of_the_Gaza_war_on_children_in_the_Gaza_Strip_france24live20231213-538)[\[527\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis#cite_note-539) As a result of the war, many children had sustained amputations and other permanent disabilities, as well as psychological trauma. Thousands more suffered from dehydration, malnutrition, diseases linked to the lack of clean water such as [gastroenteritis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastroenteritis "Gastroenteritis"), and respiratory diseases. In addition to killing people directly through traumatic injuries, wars cause "indirect deaths" by destroying, damaging, or causing deterioration of economic, social, psychological and health conditions. Most expansively, this report describes the causal pathways that can be expected to lead to far larger numbers of indirect deaths. These deaths result from diseases and other population-level health effects that stem from war's destruction of public infrastructure and livelihood sources, reduced access to water and sanitation, environmental damage, and other such factors. This report builds on a foundation of previous Costs of War research for its framework and methodology in covering the most significant chains of impact, or causal pathways, to indirect war deaths in Gaza and the West Bank. Unlike in combat, these deaths do not necessarily occur immediately or in the close aftermath of the battles which many observers focus on. While it will take years to assess the full extent of these population-level health effects, they will inevitably lead to far higher numbers of deaths than direct violence. 115.
